🎙
President of Russia
Vladimir Putin
addressed
a meeting of the BRICS Business Forum
(New Delhi, September 11, 2026)
💬
Vladimir Putin:
Friends, Prime Minister Modi, colleagues – heads of state, our friends in the audience, and members of our countries’ business community.
As per tradition, this event takes place before the BRICS Summit. Its high-profile attendance underscores
growing interest in strengthening contacts
throughout the territory of our association.
It is clear that strong economic partnerships and r
eliable business ties
largely shape the basis of international relations, reinforcing their stability and helping us overcome the crisis elements the modern world is facing.
The world has entered
a period of deep structural shifts
caused by the fact that the old leaders – relatively speaking old – who were at the forefront of economic growth in the latter half of the past century, are being replaced with
new growth drivers
. <...>
Over the past five years, as it has already been said today – I think it was our Indonesian colleague who said it, the
#BRICS
countries accounted for
over 40 percent of global GDP
, while the contribution of
the Group of Seven
, the so-called leading economies, although I don’t understand why they are called “leading,” was just 29 percent.
As for global economic growth over the same period, our association accounted for nearly half of it, while the G7 contributed just 18 percent.
What drives these trends? The answer is quite simple:
the BRICS countries
, which are home to roughly
half the world's population
, have
vast and dynamic domestic markets
. Our cities are growing and developing rapidly, urbanisation is advancing quickly, and our national companies are increasingly making their mark as global players. <...>
We have long been told that competition is
an inviolable principle
; yet, regrettably, Western competitors today are resorting to every conceivable means to reclaim their erstwhile dominance. They go so far as to employ
instruments of direct physical force
, including the destruction of industrial and logistical infrastructure, pipelines, and similar facilities.
Efforts are underway
to block international transport corridors
, to seize sea‑going vessels, while illegal restrictions are imposed, accompanied by threats of so‑called secondary sanctions, on those who refuse to act in the interests of others and instead seek to defend their own national interests.
I know my colleagues could cite hundreds of such examples of this, but consider this:
over 30 000 sanctions
have been imposed on Russia – nearly twice as many as against all other countries in the world combined. <...>
We must also acknowledge another fact: the countries that initiated this sanctions pressure, and which are now grappling with serious problems such as budget deficits, mounting public debt and industrial decline, have been unable to do the same.
👉
It turns out that they are the ones facing complex and severe consequences
. This is are not mere speculation; these are facts drawn from their own statistics. <...>
Russia is open to interesting and promising initiatives in industry, trade and tourism. We are ready to contribute to the world’s energy and food security together with our partners, and to jointly shape reliable global routes, such as
the Trans-Arctic Transport Corridor
and
the North-South International Corridor
.
Through the combined efforts of the bodies of power, businesses and expert community, BRICS is creating
a new stable platform of global growth
. It is notable that its key elements, the operating rules for companies and organisations are not imposed from the outside by the so-called golden billion. Likewise, we do not impose anything on others.
Our rules are based on
innovative business approaches
, breakthrough technological solutions, highlighting the national interests of our states and nations.

🏰
On September 11, 1812, the Russian settlement of
Fort Ross
was established on the northwestern coast of the continental United States.
It was
the first European settlement
and a fortress on the coast of Northern California located 80 km north of San Francisco. It marked
the southernmost point in North America
reached by Russian pioneers.
In the 18th century, Russian industrialists, hunters and farmers began exploring Alaska and the Aleutian Islands. Settlements began to spring up all along America’s northwestern coast. These places would later become known as Russian America.
🧭
The harsh climate of Alaska made farming difficult, and food shortages began to be felt. To address this problem,
Alexander Baranov
(1790-1818), the first chief administrator of the Russian settlements in America, sent several exploratory expeditions led by his closest aide and associate
Ivan Kuskov
(1765–1823) to California.
Ivan Kuskov spotted a plateau 30 km north of Rumyantsev Bay (present-day Bodega Bay), which was separated from the surrounding area by deep ravines and surrounded by valuable timber forests and grazing land. Kuskov purchased the plot from the Native Americans for three blankets, three pairs of trousers, two axes, three hoes, and several strings of beads. He named the nearby river the Slavyanka (the Russian River).
🇷🇺
From March to September 1812, construction work was carried out on the newly acquired land, and a fortress and a settlement were built. On August 30 (September 11), the flag of the Russian-American Company –
the Russian tricolour
bearing the imperial double-headed eagle - was raised at Fort Ross.
In a short time, orchards and vegetable gardens were planted, and farmers began raising livestock and poultry. Our ancestors hunted sea otters and sea lions that inhabited the coastal waters. Fort Ross thus became
the main source of food supplies
for the Russian settlements in Alaska.
Maritime industries also developed. The fortress had a shipyard and a boatbuilding workshop. California’s windmills and shipyards
appeared first
at Fort Ross.
The population was ethnically diverse: Russians lived side by side with Native Americans and Aleuts. The settlers not only got along with the local population, but also provided them with
basic education
and
professional skills
, and many Native Americans at Fort Ross became carpenters, blacksmiths, and shipbuilders.
☦️
The fortress was also home to
California’s first Orthodox church building
, namely,
the Chapel of the Holy Trinity
, which remains an important historical, cultural, and religious centre for San Francisco’s Russian-speaking community.
By 1841, the food supply problem in Alaska had been resolved by other means, and Fort Ross was deemed operating at a loss. The colony’s lands were sold to the “Emperor of California,” American businessman and landowner
John Sutter
. The last Russian settlers returned home in 1847, and in 1867 the United States purchased Alaska.
🕰
Today, a museum dedicated to the history of the Russian colony and the daily life and traditions of its settlers is open on the site of the former fortress. It also displays a replica of the flag presented by
Emperor Paul I
to the Russian-American Company. Located on the picturesque Pacific coast, Fort Ross attracts visitors from around the world.
These historic sites also inspired the plot of the famous opera
“Juno and Avos”
by
Alexey Rybnikov
, inspiring future generations to create artistic works, including the well-known
portrait of Concepción (Conchita) Argüello
by Russian artist
Anatoly Sokolov
, which was donated by the artist’s family to the State Historical Museum in Moscow in September 2001.
This year, the Fort Ross Historical Park hosted a
Russian cultural heritage festival
for the first time in six years
. The programme included performances of folk songs, Russian food tasting, and demonstrations of traditional crafts, as well as a traditional Russian round dance to the music played on ancient instruments.
#HistoryOfRussia

item.content:encoded:
Original source: https://t.me/MFARussia/31966

🎙
Foreign Minister
Sergey Lavrov
’s
interview
with the RBC television channel for a documentary marking the
anniversary of the tragic events of September 11, 2001
(Moscow, September 11, 2026)
❓
Question: September 11, 2001, fell on a Tuesday. The working day had only just begun. The clock read 8:45 AM when the first aircraft struck the World Trade Centre. How did you learn about these events? Where were you at that time? What was your immediate personal reaction?
💬
Sergey Lavrov
: I was in my office. The office of the Permanent Representative to the United Nations is a soundproofed room, equipped with specialised apparatus around the perimeter designed to suppress any sound, ensuring that nothing “escapes” the room. I walked to work, arriving at approximately 9 AM. <...>
My routine was always to sit at my desk. To the right of it stood a television set. I would switch it on to a news channel – at that time, it was CNN. The sound was muted. Out of the corner of my eye, I noticed an aircraft collide with a skyscraper and explode. My initial thought, at 9 AM, was that they were broadcasting some horror film. I carried on working, but something lingered in my mind. I began watching more closely and then understood the reality of what was unfolding. <...>
❓
Question: Were you not afraid to venture outside afterwards?
💬
Sergey Lavrov
: Not at all. I always walked both to and from work. <...>
After September 11, I passed those same little restaurants; the tables remained, but the entire mood had changed – people were glancing nervously over their shoulders,
a great deal had altered
.
President
Vladimir Putin
telephoned then-US President
George W. Bush
and affirmed that we stood with them. Subsequently, an appropriate resolution was adopted in the UN Security Council.
❓
Question: We have spoken about public assistance. Twenty-five years have passed. Was there any non-public assistance extended by Russia to America that can now be disclosed?
💬
Sergey Lavrov
: The Russia – NATO Council, which had already been established by that time, endorsed an entire programme concerning Afghanistan.
Our helicopters were made available for the use of the international coalitio
n. Intelligence data were shared.
❓
Question: How did international relations evolve as a consequence of these events? What does this signify for you? In your view, what was the gravest error in the new order?
💬
Sergey Lavrov
:
Relations deteriorated
. Firstly, the United States exploited this international solidarity and the resolution which authorised its military operation and the establishment of an international coalition not so much to combat terrorism as
to pursue its own geopolitical objectives
and to broaden its presence and sway.
This trend subsequently manifested itself in a number of other theatres. Prior to Afghanistan, there was Yugoslavia – an
unprovoked act of aggression and the senseless destruction of a sovereign state
. <...>
Then there was Georgia. There was Ukraine, which we also discussed. Regrettably,
this was an attempt by the unipolar world to cling to the course of historical processes
. This will persist for a considerable time. This is an entire epoch.
❓
Question: Summing up the events of September 11, 2001, how would you describe – in a single sentence – what actually happened in New York on that day?
💬
Sergey Lavrov
: I am not inclined towards conspiracy theories. I am aware of them. <...> Yet, on a purely practical level, an enormous number of individuals would have had to be involved. I cannot accept that with Americans – from whom everything “leaks” – nothing would ever have surfaced in the public domain. <...>
We maintain dialogue with the US. We engage with all who approach us. This does not mean that we agree with everyone on every issue. US President
Donald Trump
and Russian President
Vladimir Putin
have both always maintained that they are ready to listen to each other, without any preconditions.
This is the essence of politics and the essence of diplomacy.

#OTD

years ago, on
September 10, 1721
, the
#TreatyOfNystad
was signed between Russia and Sweden, having finalised the Great Northern War of 1700-1721, secured our country's
access to the Baltic Sea and granted the status of a great power.
This document — regarded as
one of the greatest achievements of Peter I
— cemented the monumental military-political and diplomatic successes of the Russian state based on the outcome of a more than 20-year-long confrontation in the Baltic region.
Russia became a leading European power
, thanks to the efforts taken by the state and the people, clever military commanders, the heroism of sailors and soldiers, and talented diplomats. On behalf of Russia, the Treaty of Nystad was signed by Count
Yakov
(James)
Bruce
, General-Feldzeugmeister and President of the Berg and Manufactory Colleges, and
Andrey
Osterman
, member of the Foreign Affairs College (
👉
read more
about that outstanding statesman and diplomat in our
in-depth biopic
).
Under the Treaty of Nystad,
Russia gained access to the Baltic Sea
, and hence to the world’s ocean and its trade routes, and
regained its former north-western territories
, including Ingria (Izhora) and part of Karelia.
Peter the Great wrote in a letter to Russian diplomat Prince Vasily Dolgoruky that the long war was a kind of a 'school', and expressed satisfaction with its outcome:
It lasted three times as long as it could, but thankfully, ended better than we could expect.
Russia also took over the Baltic territories previously seized by Sweden —
Livonia
with the city of
Riga
, and
Estonia
with the cities of
Revel
(now Tallinn) and Narva
.
That Baltic region suffered more than other territories under the Swedish rule.
Stockholm turned it into its raw materials supplier and ruthlessly exploited the local population.
In the Russian Empire, the Baltic peoples managed to recover,
preserve their identity and languages
, and also created conditions for the region’s development. By the middle of the 19th century, the population of Livonia and Estonia increased tenfold, to 350'000 and 450'000 respectively.
***
👑
As part of the celebrations of the Treaty of Nystad, on November 2, 1721, Tsar Peter
accepted the title
of
“Father of the Motherland, Emperor of All Russia, Peter the Great”
in the Church of the Holy Trinity in St. Petersburg.
The Russian state became an Empire.
📜
#ArchivesSpeak
:
The original copy of the Treaty
is kept in the Archive of Foreign Policy of the Russian Empire (AVPRI) of the Foreign Ministry of Russia.
#HistoryOfDiplomacy

🎙
Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova’s
response to a media question
regarding statements by members of Israel's Cabinet on Palestine
(September 10, 2026)
❓
Question: In recent days, several members of the Israeli Government have threatened the physical elimination of the leadership of the Palestinian National Authority and the complete annexation of the Palestinian territories, with the Arab population expelled from them. How would you comment on this?
💬
Maria Zakharova:
We have taken note of the statements you mentioned.
We link the increasingly tough rhetoric from senior Israeli officials to the electoral campaign gathering momentum
ahead of
Israel’s parliamentary elections
scheduled for October 27.
However, we believe that
the race for votes cannot justify provocative statements
that further fuel an atmosphere of mutual hostility and intolerance between Palestinians and Israelis.
❗️
We call on the parties to the conflict to act responsibly and refrain from steps that could lead to further escalation.
We consistently advocate constructive approaches
aimed at creating the necessary conditions for the resumption of direct Palestinian-Israeli dialogue on all outstanding issues.
👉
We remain convinced that there is no alternative to a comprehensive and just settlement of
the
Palestinian issue
on the well-known international legal basis
, providing for the establishment of an independent, viable and territorially contiguous
State of Palestine
, coexisting with Israel in peace and security.
Only the implementation of this formula can guarantee lasting peace for all peoples of the Middle East.

item.title: 🕯 On September 9, Russia observed the Day of Remembrance for Russian Soldiers Fallen in the Defence of Sevastopol and the Crimean War of 1853-1856
item.description: 🕯 On September 9, Russia observed the Day of Remembrance for Russian Soldiers Fallen in the Defence of Sevastopol and the Crimean War of 1853-1856 . It was on this day that the heroic 349-day defence of Sevastopol came to an end. Following the Ottoman declaration of war on Russia on October 16, 1853, active hostilities unfolded on land and at sea around the Crimean Peninsula. In an attempt to save the Ottoman Empire from defeat, particularly after the Russian fleet under Vice Admiral Pavel Nakhimov routed the Turkish squadron at the Battle of Sinop , Britain and France entered the war on Turkiye’s side. In 1854, allied troops landed in Crimea and began the siege of Sevastopol . The city’s defence was led by outstanding Russian military commanders, including Vladimir Kornilov and Pavel Nakhimov . Among its defenders was the great writer Leo Tolstoy , who later recounted his experiences in his Sevastopol Sketches . Sevastopol’s defenders held the city for almost a year , skilfully and selflessly repelling assaults by superior enemy forces. After prolonged and fierce fighting, Russian troops withdrew in an orderly manner from the southern side of Sevastopol. The army retained its fighting capability, and the allies never succeeded in forcing its surrender. ⚔️ The defence of Sevastopol became a symbol of the courage, resilience and military valour of Russian soldiers and sailors. *** The memory of Sevastopol’s heroic Russian defenders apparently remains a sore point for those for

, skilfully and selflessly repelling assaults by superior enemy forces.
After prolonged and fierce fighting, Russian troops withdrew in an orderly manner from the southern side of Sevastopol.
The army retained its fighting capability, and the allies never succeeded in forcing its surrender.
⚔️
The defence of Sevastopol became a symbol of the courage, resilience and military valour of Russian soldiers and sailors.
***
The memory of Sevastopol’s heroic Russian defenders apparently
remains a sore point
for those for whom the Crimean War serves as a reminder of a gruelling and bloody campaign.
On June 10, 2026, the Kiev regime
deliberately launched a drone attack
on
the Defence of Sevastopol, 1854-1855 Panorama Museum
.
Severe damage
was inflicted on
Franz Roubaud’s world-famous painting The Assault of June 6, 1855
, depicting Russian troops repelling an assault on Malakhov Hill by superior British and French forces.
According to Russia’s Foreign Intelligence Service
,
the attack on the museum was a meticulously planned provocation orchestrated by London and British intelligence services
, while Ukrainian military personnel carried out the preparations and launched the drones.
👉
But no provocation can change the truth
: the Russian soldier’s resilience will forever remain part of history, while Britain’s gruelling military campaign and enormous losses are immortalised in the famous panorama.

item.title: 🗓 #Announcement On September 11-13, President of Russia Vladimir Putin will pay a working visit to India
item.description: #Announcement 🗓 On September 11-13, President of Russia Vladimir Putin will pay a working visit to India to attend the XVIII BRICS Summit . The event will take place in New Delhi as #BRICS marks its 20th anniversary . On September 11, Vladimir Putin will address the Plenary Session of the annual BRICS Business Forum , which traditionally precedes the Summit and serves as an important platform for dialogue among business representatives from BRICS countries. On the same day, Russia's President will hold a bilateral meeting with Prime Minister of India Narendra Modi and join him for a visit to the Innoprom exhibition , organised by the two countries’ Ministries of Industry and Trade. The main Summit programme will begin on September 12 with a meeting of BRICS Leaders to discuss initiatives put forward by the Indian Chairship and prospects for further strengthening the BRICS strategic partnership in politics and security, economics and finance, and cultural and humanitarian ties. The Leaders will also exchange views on current international and regional issues. On September 13, an expanded BRICS meeting will bring together the Heads of delegations from BRICS member and partner countries, as well as invited countries and Heads of international organisations. ✍️ The key agreements reached are expected to be reflected in the Summit’s final document . During the events in New Delhi, Vladimir Putin will also hold a number of other bilateral meetings . #RussiaIndia #DruzhbaDosti #BRIC
